title.en: Stored in a Famous Mountain: From the Letter to Ren An

edition.en: Three paragraphs of the letter as quoted in Sima Qian’s biography in the History of the Former Han (Han shu, chapter 62), from Chinese Wikisource; checked against the Wen xuan text of the letter (Wikisource, 報任少卿書), which differs in a few words.
edition.zh: 据维基文库所录《汉书·司马迁传》（卷六十二）中引录的书信，节选三段；并与《文选》本（维基文库《报任少卿书》）对校，两本有个别字句不同。

basis.en: Written about 91 BCE; the author died about 86 BCE.
basis.zh: 约作于公元前 91 年，作者约卒于公元前 86 年。

note.en: Sima Qian wrote this letter to his friend Ren An after he had suffered the palace punishment for speaking up for a defeated general, while the history his father had charged him to write was still unfinished. These paragraphs give his reason for living on: the lasting books of the past were written by people in trouble, who recounted past events and thought of those to come. He means to store his own book in a famous mountain and pass it to the people who will understand it. Notice how exactly he pictures his reader: not his own age, but someone later, wherever they turn out to be.
note.zh: 司马迁因替一位战败的将军说话而受了宫刑，父亲托付给他的那部史书还没有完成，这时他给朋友任安写了这封信。这几段说的是他为什么活下去：古来流传的书，多是人在困厄中写成的，他们“述往事，思来者”。他要把自己的书“藏之名山，传之其人”。请留意他对读者的想象有多么确切：不是同时代的人，而是后来的某个人，不论那人在哪里。

pick.en: I keep this letter for one phrase, 述往事，思來者: recount what has happened, and think of those who are to come. It is the best short account I know of what a library is for. I also keep it because he says plainly whom he is writing for, the right reader, later, and that is the reader I hope these shelves find.
pick.zh: 我留下这封信，是为了一句话：“述往事，思来者。”在我知道的说法里，这是对图书馆用途最好的简短说明。我也留下它，是因为他清楚地说出了自己为谁而写：后来的、对的那位读者。这也是我希望这些书架能遇到的读者。

excerpt.orig: 此人皆意有所鬱結，不得通其道，故述往事，思來者。
excerpt.en: These men all had something knotted in their hearts that they could not carry through, so they recounted past events and thought of those to come.
excerpt.zh: 此人皆意有所郁结，不得通其道，故述往事，思来者。

gloss.en: 函, to be held in or sunk in: ‘sunk in dung and dirt’, living on in disgrace.
gloss.zh: 函，包含、陷身。陷身于粪土之中，指忍辱偷生。

gloss.at: 鄙沒世而文采不表於後
gloss.at_hans: 鄙没世而文采不表于后
gloss.en: 鄙, to be ashamed of; 沒世, to come to the end of one’s life. The Wen xuan text reads 鄙陋沒世，而文采不表於後世.
gloss.zh: 鄙，以……为耻；没世，终了一生。《文选》本作“鄙陋没世，而文采不表于后世”。

gloss.en: Free and extraordinary, not bound by the common measure.
gloss.zh: 俶傥：卓异不凡，不受拘束。

gloss.en: The Lord of the West, later honoured as King Wen of Zhou, was held at Youli by the last Shang king; tradition says he worked out the sixty-four hexagrams there.
gloss.zh: 西伯即周文王。相传他被商纣王囚于羑里，推演出六十四卦。

gloss.en: Confucius was stranded and in want between Chen and Cai on his travels; late in life he edited the Spring and Autumn Annals of Lu.
gloss.zh: 孔子周游列国时困于陈、蔡之间；晚年修订鲁国史书《春秋》。

gloss.en: Qu Yuan (c. 340–278 BCE), banished from the court of Chu, wrote ‘Encountering Sorrow’, the long poem at the head of the Chu ci.
gloss.zh: 屈原（约前 340—前 278）被楚王放逐，作《离骚》，为《楚辞》之首。

gloss.en: Zuo Qiuming, traditionally said to have been blind, is the reputed author of the Discourses of the States.
gloss.zh: 左丘明，相传失明，旧说《国语》为他所作。

gloss.en: Sun Bin, whose kneecaps were cut out at the instigation of his rival Pang Juan; a book of strategy under his name was rediscovered in a tomb in 1972.
gloss.zh: 孙膑，被同学庞涓陷害，受膑刑（去膝盖骨）。题为他所作的兵书于 1972 年在汉墓中重新发现。

gloss.en: Lü Buwei, chancellor of Qin, was ordered into exile in Shu; the Lü shi chunqiu he sponsored had in fact been compiled before then. Sima Qian is citing the pattern, not the dates.
gloss.zh: 吕不韦，秦相，被贬迁蜀；他主持编成的《吕氏春秋》其实成书于此之前。司马迁在这里举的是大概，不是年份。

gloss.en: Han Fei died in prison in Qin in 233 BCE; ‘The Difficulties of Persuasion’ and ‘Solitary Indignation’ are chapters of the Han Feizi.
gloss.zh: 韩非于公元前 233 年死于秦国狱中；《说难》《孤愤》是《韩非子》中的篇目。

gloss.en: The same as 大抵: for the most part.
空文, ‘empty writing’: words, as opposed to deeds; 垂, to hand down; 自見, to make oneself seen.
gloss.zh: 空文，指文章著述（相对于事功而言）；垂，流传；自见，表现自己。

gloss.en: Old records and reports that had been scattered and lost.
The Shiji (Records of the Grand Historian) has 130 chapters.

gloss.at: 究天人之際，通古今之變，成一家之言
gloss.at_hans: 究天人之际，通古今之变，成一家之言
gloss.en: The most quoted statement of the historian’s aim: to search out where heaven and the human meet, to see through the changes of past and present, and to found a school of one’s own.
gloss.zh: 这是史家宗旨最常被引用的表述：探究天道与人事的关系，贯通古今的变化，自成一家的学说。

gloss.en: Here the palace punishment he had suffered, reckoned the heaviest short of death.
gloss.zh: 这里指他所受的宫刑，被视为仅次于死刑的重刑。

gloss.en: To store it in a famous mountain and pass it to the people fit to receive it. In his own afterword he adds that a copy was kept in the capital.
gloss.zh: 藏在名山之中，传给合适的人。他在《太史公自序》中还说，副本留在京师。

gloss.en: Towns on the great roads and the large cities: wherever the book could circulate.
gloss.zh: 四通八达的城邑和大都会，指书得以流布的地方。

marginalia.en: Two clauses, one facing back and one facing forward. Most of what stands on this shelf lives in the space between them.
marginalia.zh: 两个分句，一个朝后，一个朝前。这个书架上的大部分东西，都住在它们之间。

marginalia.en: A plan with redundancy in it: one copy put away somewhere safe, others handed to readers. People who look after archives still work this way.
marginalia.zh: 这是一个带有冗余的计划：一份放在安全的地方，另一些交到读者手里。今天照管档案的人，仍然这样做。

marginalia.en: He uses 空文, ‘empty writing’, without contempt. When deeds are no longer possible, writing is what is left that can still act.
marginalia.zh: 他说“空文”，并无轻视之意。当行事已不可能时，剩下仍能起作用的，就是文字。

note.en: One of the great letters in any language: the historian explains why he chose disgrace over death to finish his book, and for whom, the reader still to come.
note.zh: 任何语言里最伟大的书信之一：史家说明为何宁受屈辱也要写完这部书，又为谁而写：那尚未到来的读者。
